title: Mount Everest's Name
passages: Mount Everest is named after Sir George Everest, a Welsh SURVEYOR who led the mapping of India from 1830 to 1843. Oddly, he never saw the mountain, and he even objected when the Royal Geographical Society gave it his name in 1865. He said his own name as "Eve rest," not the way most people say it today. Long before then, people living near the peak had their own names for it. In Tibet it is called CHOMOLUNGMA, often translated as "Goddess Mother of the World." In Nepal it is SAGARMATHA, which can mean "Forehead of the Sky."

At first, surveyors listed the peak simply as Peak XV. Around 1852, their careful measurements showed it was the tallest mountain on Earth. Today its official height is 8,848.86 meters, or about 29,032 feet, a figure that Nepal and China announced together in 2020. Reaching the top took many attempts. On 29 May 1953, Edmund Hillary from New Zealand and Tenzing Norgay, a Sherpa climber, finally stood on the SUMMIT as part of a British EXPEDITION. They stayed there for only about 15 minutes. Since then, more than 6,000 people have made the climb, many guided by Sherpa families who know these mountains well.
